description: In November 2025, a hacker using the name ellie.191 gained unauthorized access to Suno systems and obtained outdated source code, internal details about the company's music-scraping and model-training pipelines, customer account information, and Stripe purchase data. The actor said a Suno employee had been compromised through the Shai-Hulud supply-chain worm and that harvested GitHub and cloud credentials enabled the intrusion; the actor's relationship to the original Shai-Hulud campaign is unknown. Have I Been Pwned later examined a dataset containing 55.3 million unique email addresses, some phone numbers, and tens of thousands of purchase records with names, addresses, transaction information, and partial card details. Suno confirmed a November 2025 incident and did not dispute the reported account count, although it said the incident primarily involved outdated source code and that no sensitive personal information was compromised. No operational disruption was reported.
